economy.spending_outlays.plain: For the federal grants and contracts signed for work in Puerto Rico in each federal fiscal year since 2020, how much was committed over each award's life and how much the federal Treasury has paid out to the recipients so far, by function. It shows how far the money has gone, not what it achieved.
economy.spending_outlays.definition: spending_outlays.json holds, for the grants and contracts with place of performance Puerto Rico that USAspending.gov lists as signed in each federal fiscal year (October to September) from 2020, the sum of each award's obligation over its life and of its total outlays to date, by program (assistance listing) or, for contracts, by awarding agency, with the program's function. An award's outlays count up to its obligated amount; the excess and the awards with no outlay reported are counted apart.
economy.spending_outlays.method: federal_outlays.py asks USAspending.gov's award search for every grant (award types 02 to 05) and contract (A to D) with place of performance Puerto Rico signed in each federal fiscal year from 2020, with its Award Amount (obligation over the award's life) and Total Outlays. USAspending has outlays from fiscal year 2020, so older awards are not read. Each program takes its function from the function crosswalk; a contract takes its awarding agency's default. FEMA Public Assistance (97.036) is left out.
economy.spending_outlays.how_to_read: Read the share paid out of each function or signing year: a low share means money committed and not yet paid to the recipients, which is usual for large multi-year grants such as disaster recovery. Older signing years have had more time to pay out.
economy.spending_outlays.geography: Puerto Rico as a whole (place of performance Puerto Rico)

economy.unused_funds.plain: For the federal grants signed for work in Puerto Rico since federal fiscal year 2020 that ended more than a year ago, how many still show money that was committed and not paid, and how much, by federal agency and by program. A balance on record is not money lost, and by itself it does not show that money is at risk.
economy.unused_funds.definition: unused_funds.json holds, for the grants with place of performance Puerto Rico that USAspending.gov lists as signed in each federal fiscal year (October to September) from 2020, the count and the dollars of the ones whose end date is more than one year before the day the data were read and whose obligation exceeds their total outlays by at least 5% of the award and at least $1,000, by awarding federal agency, by assistance listing and by the year they ended. Medicaid is kept apart and FEMA Public Assistance is left out.
economy.unused_funds.method: unused_funds.py asks USAspending.gov's award search for every grant (award types 02 to 05) with place of performance Puerto Rico signed in each federal fiscal year from 2020, with its Award Amount (obligation over the award's life), its Total Outlays and its End Date. An award has ended when its end date is more than one year before the read date: the 120 days a recipient has to draw down (2 CFR 200.344) and the agency's year to close the award have passed. The unpaid balance is the obligation minus the outlays, never below zero. Ended awards that report no outlay are counted apart and not as unpaid.
economy.unused_funds.how_to_read: Read the number of grants next to the dollars: one large grant can put a program or an agency near the top. Older end years are less likely to be paid.
economy.unused_funds.geography: Puerto Rico as a whole (place of performance Puerto Rico)

view.label: Knowledge Area: Federal grants: balances, reductions and audit findings

economy.spending_federal.plain: What federal agencies committed to spend on work or benefits in Puerto Rico in each federal fiscal year: Social Security and Medicare payments, Medicaid and nutrition grants, education and housing grants, federal contracts and more. Each program is sorted by what it pays for (health, social services, education and so on). It is island-wide: the municipio figures are in the federal awards series of the Analysis tab.
economy.spending_federal.definition: spending_federal.json holds, for each federal fiscal year (October to September, named by the year it ends), USAspending.gov's obligations with place of performance Puerto Rico. Each row is one assistance listing (program) and award type (grants, direct payments, loans, other) or, for contracts, one awarding agency, with its function, the confidence of that function and its whole dollars in each year. Programs under $1 million in every year are added into one 'Other programs' row per agency, award type and function. totals is USAspending's own sum per year and award type; the rows add up to it.
economy.spending_federal.method: federal_awards.py asks USAspending.gov's API (spending_by_category) for the obligations with place of performance Puerto Rico in each finished federal fiscal year, once for each award type: assistance by assistance listing, contracts by awarding agency. Each listing takes its function from the function crosswalk (dictionary_src/spending_crosswalk.csv), or else its agency's default function (low confidence); a contract takes its awarding agency's default. Loans are the estimated cost to the government, not the amount lent.
economy.spending_federal.how_to_read: Compare the functions of one year, or one function across years. An obligation is a commitment to pay, recorded when the award is made or changed, so a large multi-year grant can show up in a single year.
economy.spending_federal.geography: Puerto Rico as a whole (place of performance Puerto Rico)

economy.spending_fema_pa.plain: How much of FEMA's disaster Public Assistance in Puerto Rico is in projects that are closed out, open or waiting for a review, and how long the open money has been open, for the whole island, each disaster and each municipio. It shows where to ask, not whether a project failed.
economy.spending_fema_pa.definition: spending_fema_pa.json holds OpenFEMA's Public Assistance projects in Puerto Rico summed by process step (closed out, open, pending a review), with the federal share obligated in dollars, the dollar-weighted median years since each open project's first obligation, and the dollars open more than five years; island-wide, by disaster, by damage category and by municipio. Projects recorded as Statewide are summed apart.
economy.spending_fema_pa.method: fema_pa_stage.py reads every Puerto Rico row of OpenFEMA's Public Assistance Funded Projects Details: its process step, federal share obligated, first obligation date, disaster, damage category and county code. Closed is Project Closed Out; open is Obligated; pending is any Pending step. Age counts from the first obligation to the day the data were read.
economy.spending_fema_pa.how_to_read: Compare the share closed out and the age of what is open between municipios or disasters. A large share of old open money points to where to ask; large permanent works take years.
economy.spending_fema_pa.geography: Municipio, with the projects recorded as Statewide apart

economy.spending_municipio.plain: For each municipio, in one place: the capital plan's projects there and the agencies that run them, the disaster recovery subawards and FEMA projects that name it, with how long FEMA money has been open and how much is closed out, and the federal awards in its territory. It counts only the money that names the municipio.
economy.spending_municipio.definition: spending_municipio.json gathers, for each of the 78 municipios, figures the observatory already publishes elsewhere: the capital plan for its four fiscal years and its three largest agencies (spending_pica.json), the CDBG-DR and CDBG-MIT subawards (spending_cdbgdr.json), FEMA Public Assistance by stage with the median age of open money and the dollars open more than five years (spending_fema_pa.json), and federal awards of every type in the latest federal fiscal year and the average of the last five (economy_series.json), with the slug of its ABRE Tu Municipio page.
economy.spending_municipio.method: municipio_view.py reads the four published files and writes one row per municipio; it adds no source and changes no figure.
economy.spending_municipio.how_to_read: Read the parts side by side, not added: they are different stages (planned, obligated) and some are the same money (FEMA Public Assistance is also in the federal awards).

economy.audit_findings.plain: How many problems the yearly audits of federal money found in bodies in Puerto Rico since 2019, and how many of them the auditor marked as repeated from the audit before, by year, kind of body, federal agency and program. A repeated finding is the closest open measure of whether a problem was corrected.
economy.audit_findings.definition: audit_findings.json holds, for the single audits that bodies in Puerto Rico filed in the Federal Audit Clearinghouse from audit year 2019, the number of audits, of audits with at least one finding on a federal program, of findings, and of findings that are repeated, a material weakness or carry questioned costs, by audit year, by the kind of body the Clearinghouse records, by federal agency and by assistance listing; and, by year, the audits accepted more than nine months after the fiscal year ended.
economy.audit_findings.method: audit_findings.py asks the Federal Audit Clearinghouse API for the audits with auditee state PR from audit year 2019, then for their findings and for their award lines with a finding. The API lists a finding once per award line; the script counts one finding per audit and reference number, with a flag set when any of its lines sets it. In the breakdowns by agency and by program a finding counts once in each agency or program it touches.
economy.audit_findings.how_to_read: Read the share repeated next to the number of findings: programs with many audited bodies have more findings. The two latest audit years are incomplete, because audits arrive late.
economy.audit_findings.geography: Puerto Rico as a whole (bodies whose audit gives a Puerto Rico address)

economy.spending_cdbg.plain: Where HUD's yearly Community Development Block Grant money went in Puerto Rico, by municipio and federal fiscal year: the entitlement grants HUD pays straight to 27 larger municipios, and the subawards of the CDBG state program that the Puerto Rico Department of Housing passes to the other municipios.
economy.spending_cdbg.definition: spending_cdbg.json holds, for each federal fiscal year (October to September), the obligations of the CDBG entitlement grants (assistance listing 14.218, grant code MC) by the municipio that receives them (entitlement) and for Puerto Rico (entitlement_total), and the first-tier subawards that USAspending.gov reports under the CDBG state program grant (14.228, grant code DC) by the municipio of the place of performance (state_by_muni), those that name no municipio (state_unplaced), their total (state_subawards) and the state grant's obligations (state_prime), in dollars. The grant numbers are in awards.
economy.spending_cdbg.method: cdbg_regular.py reads the entitlement grant numbers from USAspending.gov's award search and asks its API (spending_by_geography) for each final federal fiscal year: the entitlement grants by municipio and for Puerto Rico, the state program's subawards by municipio and for Puerto Rico, and the state grant for Puerto Rico. The disaster grants (CDBG-DR, CDBG-MIT, in spending_cdbgdr.json) and the COVID grants (CDBG-CV) are left out.
economy.spending_cdbg.how_to_read: Each municipio gets either an entitlement grant or state program subawards (Trujillo Alto had both in different years). Compare municipios per resident over the same years, and read the latest year with care: subawards often arrive a year or more after the grant.
economy.spending_cdbg.geography: Municipio, with the subawards that name no municipio apart
